title: ICC issues arrest warrants for Netanyahu, Gallant and Mohammed Deif
body:
On 21 November 2024, a pre-trial chamber of the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, former Israeli defence minister Yoav Gallant, who had been replaced earlier that month, and Hamas military commander Mohammed Deif. The judges found reasonable grounds to believe that Netanyahu and Gallant bear criminal responsibility for the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare, and for the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution and other inhumane acts. They were also accused of intentionally directing attacks against civilians as civilian superiors.

For Deif, the judges found reasonable grounds to believe he was responsible for crimes against humanity, including murder, extermination, torture and rape, and for war crimes such as hostage-taking and cruel treatment, relating to the 7 October 2023 attack. The Israeli military says Deif was killed in an air strike in July 2024, but the court said the prosecution could not determine whether he was dead or alive.

The chamber rejected Israel's challenges to the court's jurisdiction. Enforcement falls to the ICC's 124 member states; Israel and the United States are not members. Israeli President Isaac Herzog condemned the decision and Palestinian politician Mustafa Barghouti welcomed the warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant. Israel and Hamas both rejected the allegations.
